title: Thermodynamics

standard_text: Thermal equilibrium and definition of temperature, zeroth law of thermodynamics, heat, work and internal energy, first law of thermodynamics, isothermal and adiabatic processes, second law of thermodynamics, reversible and irreversible processes, heat engines and refrigerators.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 11 Thermodynamics: zeroth and first laws, work done by a gas, isothermal and adiabatic processes, the second law, heat engines and refrigerators. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

The zeroth law gives us temperature. The first law is energy conservation: heat supplied Q = ΔU + W, where W is the work done by the gas (pΔV at constant pressure). For an ideal gas ΔU depends only on temperature, so ΔU = 0 in an isothermal change; in an adiabatic change Q = 0 and pVγ is constant.

The second law says no engine can turn all its heat into work and heat does not flow from cold to hot by itself. The best engine between T₁ and T₂ is a Carnot engine, η = 1 − T₂/T₁; an ideal refrigerator has coefficient of performance T₂/(T₁ − T₂).

Example

Q = 800 J, W = 300 J. ΔU?

800 − 300

Answer: 500 J

Example

Carnot between 600 K and 300 K?

1 − 300/600

Answer: 50%

Common mistakes

  • Using °C in the Carnot formula.
  • Thinking an ideal engine can be 100% efficient.
  • Confusing isothermal (ΔT = 0) and adiabatic (Q = 0).

faq.q: What is the first law of thermodynamics?
faq.a: Heat supplied to a system equals the increase in internal energy plus the work done by the system: Q = ΔU + W.

faq.q: Why can no engine be 100% efficient?
faq.a: The second law says some heat must always be given out to a colder reservoir.
